# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👇]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍]

I need to figure out what Mute is trying to tell me through gestures, since Mute can't speak to me directly in a way that... wait, actually Mute *can* speak, and I *can* hear speech from Mute (speak lands on whoever comes after in turn order, and I'm last: Mute, Blind, Deaf). But this turn Mute only gestured, no speech content shown. Let me work with what I have.

The gestures seem paired: [👍 👆], [👌 👇], [✌ 👍]. This looks like it could be encoding wire-related info (numbers/directions) since I see WIRES 1/2/3 with colors. Mute has the manual and doesn't know colors, but might be asking me something or encoding instructions using a scheme established elsewhere (perhaps with Blind, whom I can't see).

Since I can't be sure what these gestures mean yet, my job is to report what I see (the bomb's display, light, and wires) so Blind and Mute can use it. I should speak to both Mute and Blind describing colors/markings, since Blind can't see and Mute can't touch — but Mute can hear me, and Blind can hear me too. That's my main value: transmitting visual info via speech.

```
speak(text="Display shows 0. Light is white. Three wires: wire 1 is green, wire 2 is blue, wire 3 is yellow.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍]

The light changed from white to orange — likely a reaction to something Blind did, or just the state. Mute keeps gesturing to me only, no speech received from Mute yet (I never receive speech anyway, only Mute and Blind do from each other/me). Mute's gestures to me: first turn had three pairs, now just [✌ 👍] repeated. This might be Mute asking me to confirm/watch for a specific state, since ✌👍 was the third pair last time too.

I can't interpret gestures with certainty, but I should keep feeding visual updates since that's my unique value. The light changing to orange is important new info - I should report it immediately.

```
speak(text="Update: light changed to orange. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👇]

The light keeps changing (white → orange → green) while display stays 0 and wires stay the same. This suggests Blind is cycling through some action (maybe pressing something) and the light is the bomb's feedback to that action, which only I can see. Mute is gesturing different pairs each turn to me — possibly trying to signal something back, but without established meaning I can't decode it, and I never receive Mute's speech to Blind or context of what's being asked.

My critical job: report the light state changes immediately and clearly, since that's likely feedback Blind needs interpreted for safety (green could mean "good/safe", orange "caution", white "neutral").

```
speak(text="Update: light is now green. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👆]

The light cycled white → orange → green → white, back to start. This matches the same pattern as turn 1's first gesture pair. Mute's gestures to me seem to correlate with the light color at that time:
- Turn 1: light white, gesture [👍 👆] (also two others sent same turn, likely all queued from turn 0)
- Turn 4: light white, gesture [👍 👆]

This matches! Turn 2: light orange, gesture [✌ 👍]. Turn 3: light green, gesture [👌 👇].

So Mute might be echoing back a code per light color that came from the manual — meaning Mute knows what each light color should correspond to via the manual, and is confirming/labeling it for me, or asking me to confirm the color matches what Blind is doing.

Since I now see white again with gesture 👍👆 repeating, this seems to be a stable mapping:
- white = 👍👆
- orange = ✌👍
- green = 👌👇

I should report this pattern back to help coordination, and confirm current state.

```
speak(text="Cycle repeated: light is white again, same as turn 1. Sequence so far: white, orange, green, white. Display 0, wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍]

Confirmed: the light is cycling white→orange→green→white→orange, and Mute's gesture to me matches exactly the same pattern as before (orange = ✌👍, matching turn 2). This strongly confirms Mute has a fixed gesture-per-color code from the manual, likely to verify I'm seeing the same color Blind's action produces, or to communicate manual instructions tied to colors that Mute can't say aloud (maybe the color names themselves are unspeakable/unpronounceable marks).

This is useful confirmation but I should keep reporting plainly so Blind (who can hear me) has accurate state info to act on.

```
speak(text="Confirmed cycle continues: light orange again, matches turn 2 pattern. Display 0, wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👇]

Pattern fully confirmed: white↔👍👆, orange↔✌👍, green↔👌👇. The cycle continues (white,orange,green,white,orange,green) with everything else static. Nothing is progressing — the wires and display never change, so likely Blind isn't taking real action yet, or this is just the natural light cycle unrelated to actions, and we're all waiting to establish communication before someone commits to cutting a wire or pressing something.

I should try to prompt progress or signal that the pattern is understood, and give Blind a clear picture to act on. Since I can't hear Blind or Mute's speech, I don't know what plan exists. I'll state my read of the situation plainly and suggest we need to identify which wire to cut, prompting whoever holds actionable info (Mute via manual) to move to instructions if pattern-confirmation is done.

```
speak(text="Pattern confirmed: white equals your gesture thumbs-up-plus-point-up, orange equals peace-plus-thumbs-up, green equals ok-sign-plus-point-down. Cycle keeps repeating, display and wires unchanged. Ready for next instruction - what should Blind do?")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

New gesture: 🤟 (love-you sign), different from the cycle-confirmation pairs before. This is likely a new signal — perhaps Mute confirming they understood my message, or signaling "go ahead" / a new instruction now that the color-code mapping is established. Since I can't ask directly and can't hear Mute, I'll treat this as acknowledgment and try to move things forward, while still reporting the current visual state accurately.

Light is back to white (full cycle: white,orange,green,white,orange,green,white). This seems purely cyclical and possibly automatic/passive, not tied to Blind's actions yet.

```
speak(text="Received a new signal from you - single gesture, different from the color cycle ones. Light is white again, display 0, wires unchanged 1 green 2 blue 3 yellow. Blind, if you take an action let us know so we can watch for a change.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Another new single gesture: ☝ (index finger up). Different from 🤟 last turn. These might be a countdown or sequence of distinct signals now that the color-mapping phase is done. Light continues cycling normally (orange, matching expected cycle position).

Let me track: turn7=🤟, turn8=☝. Could be counting up or spelling something via gesture-to-letter/number mapping known only via manual. Without more context I'll keep reporting state and flag the new gesture for the record, encouraging Blind to report any action taken since I have no way to know if Blind has done anything (nothing on the board changes).

```
speak(text="New single gesture again, different from before - looks like a sequence, not a repeat. Light orange, display 0, wires unchanged. Still no change in wires or display - Blind, has anything been tried yet?")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍]

New gesture: 👍👍👍 (three thumbs up) - triple repetition, distinct pattern again. Light continues its cycle (green, as expected). Still nothing changing on the board besides the light cycling passively.

Sequence of distinct signals so far: 🤟, ☝, 👍👍👍. Could be Mute counting or spelling out a wire number (three thumbs-up = "3"?) since ☝ could mean "1" and 🤟 might mean something else. Actually ☝ = 1 finger, 👍👍👍×3 could indicate "3". Let me consider: 🤟 doesn't map to a number obviously. Possibly these are letters via a hand-alphabet convention, or maybe counting occurrences.

I don't have enough certainty to decode this alone. I'll report faithfully and note the pattern for the group, since Blind can hear me and may have the manual context (via Mute's speech) to interpret combined with what I share.

```
speak(text="Third distinct gesture in a row, this one is thumbs-up repeated three times. Sequence so far: single sign, single sign, then triple thumbs-up. Light green, display 0, wires unchanged: 1 green 2 blue 3 yellow.")
wait()
```
